pages.text: "I'll play until the dinner bell!" Mei the timid baby goat ran on the grassy slope. Rudi the hungry squirrel chased, laughing. The far edge of the sky was growing dark.
Wind swept past, and big raindrops fell. Rumble! A loud sound came from the sky. Mei froze on the spot, unable to move.
Rudi pointed to the lodge above. "Mei, run to the lodge!" Afraid, Mei slipped under the nearest big tree. "This is closer..."
Rain poured between the leaves, soaking Mei's back. Flash! The sky turned white, then thunder rumbled again. Alone beneath the tree, Mei trembled.
High above, the friends' faces lined up at the lodge window. Inside looked warm and yellow. Mei couldn't get there.
Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, came down the slope with a big blanket over her. She wrapped Mei under it. "Not under a big tree. Lightning comes to the highest places."
Grandma held Mei's hand as they climbed the slope. "Thunder rumbles—to the lodge!" she said in time with their steps. Mei repeated, "Thunder rumbles—to the lodge!"
By the stove, Rudi offered a dry towel. Mei's wet scarf was already hung beside the stove. Holding both ends of the dry scarf, Mei smiled. "Even with thunder, I'm okay in here."
A few days later, thunder rumbled again. Mei was first to run uphill. "One, not under a tree! Two, run to the lodge! Three, hold hands, go together!" The four followed right behind Mei.
Grandma hugged Mei and dried their wet ears with a towel. Even a scary sound is okay when you know where to run. By the stove, Mei called bravely, "Thunder rumbles—to the lodge!"
